history.title: Connection history
history.confirm_clear_message: All connection history on this device will be deleted. This cannot be undone.

tunnel.no_selection: Select a tunnel or import a configuration file.
tunnel.drop_hint: Drop a .conf file, .zip file, or QR image here to import tunnels.
tunnel.import_hint: Import WireGuard configurations (.conf), ZIP files, or QR images (PNG/JPG/WebP).
tunnel.helper_recovering: Reconnecting to the VPN service. Try again shortly.
tunnel.dns_split_note: Use the tunnel’s DNS servers only for these domains. Supported on macOS and Linux with systemd-resolved. Not available on Windows.
tunnel.notes_placeholder: Add notes about the server location or tunnel’s purpose.
tunnel.resize_hint: Drag to resize · double-click to restore the default width
tunnel.health_check_override_hint: Overrides the Settings health check for this tunnel only. Reconnects the tunnel when its handshake goes stale (180 seconds). Time asleep does not count (the check pauses for 90 seconds after waking, and on macOS while offline). If the tunnel has never completed a handshake, it is reconnected only after it has sent traffic, at growing intervals.
tunnel.dns_chip_global_hint: This config requests that the tunnel’s DNS servers replace your system DNS while connected, so every name lookup goes to them.
tunnel.dns_chip_split_hint: This config requests that only these domains go to the tunnel’s DNS servers while your system DNS answers everything else. Supported on macOS and Linux with systemd-resolved; on Windows, connecting fails.
tunnel.dns_chip_search_hint: This config sets search domains but no DNS servers. It requests that your system DNS servers stay in place and the system search domains change while connected. Search domains are applied on macOS and Linux; Windows ignores them.
tunnel.dns_protected_hint: DNS protection is active: DNS to anything except this tunnel's resolvers is blocked.
tunnel.dns_intended_hint: DNS protection is turned on, but the firewall is not pinning this tunnel's DNS right now. See Settings > Advanced.

lint.dns_global_outside: {servers} is reached over your normal network, not the tunnel, and replaces system DNS on every network service while connected (DNS protection will then allow only this server). Add ~domain to scope it, or remove DNS.
lint.dns_global_outside_adapter: {servers} is reached over your normal network, not the tunnel, and is used for all DNS while connected (DNS protection will then allow only this server). Add ~domain to scope it, or remove DNS.
lint.dns_global_outside_windows: {servers} is reached over your normal network, not the tunnel, and is used for all DNS while connected (DNS protection will then allow only this server). Remove DNS, or use a server inside the tunnel's AllowedIPs.
lint.dns_mdns: ~{domain} overlaps with mDNS (.local); lookups may not reach the tunnel's DNS server. Prefer a different suffix such as .lan or .corp.
lint.dns_split_windows: Split DNS is not supported on Windows; connecting will fail. Remove the ~ entries to use the servers for all DNS.
lint.dns_split_linux: Split DNS on Linux requires systemd-resolved (resolvectl); without it connecting will fail.
lint.mtu_high: MTU {mtu} is above {max} and may fragment packets over typical 1500-byte paths.
lint.dns_lan_none: No private-name resolution: add DNS = {gateway}, ~<domain> to resolve names on the remote network.
lint.dns_lan_none_windows: No private-name resolution: add DNS = {gateway} to resolve names on the remote network. Windows then uses it for all DNS while connected; split DNS is not supported.
lint.dns_no_reverse: Split DNS has no reverse zone, so IP-to-name lookups for the remote network use system DNS. Add {zones} to resolve them through the tunnel.
lint.dns_no_reverse_limit: Split DNS has no reverse zone, so IP-to-name lookups for the remote network use system DNS. Adding {zones} would exceed the split-DNS limits (32 match and search domains, 2000-byte command), so there is no one-click fix. Remove unused domains first.
lint.cmp_tilde_info: Route only this domain (and its subdomains) to the tunnel's DNS server. All other queries keep using your system DNS. Needs at least one DNS server IP in the same line.
lint.cmp_template_info: Server, one split domain and its reverse zone. Replace corp.lan with your private domain.
lint.hover_global: DNS = 1.1.1.1 replaces system DNS while connected.
lint.hover_split: DNS = 10.0.0.1, ~corp.lan sends only corp.lan queries to the tunnel's server and leaves system DNS alone.
lint.hover_split_unsupported: Not supported on Windows: a DNS line with ~domain entries fails to connect. Use plain DNS servers instead.
lint.hover_none: No DNS line leaves system DNS untouched, so private names will not resolve through the tunnel.
lint.hover_nxdomain: A name that the tunnel's server does not know returns NXDOMAIN; there is no fallback to system DNS.
lint.hover_dig: dig queries servers directly and bypasses split DNS. To test what apps see, use dscacheutil -q host -a name <name> (macOS) or resolvectl query <name> (Linux).
lint.hover_match: Split DNS: queries for {domain} and its subdomains go to this tunnel's DNS server; everything else uses system DNS.

settings.automation_backup_recovery: A backup of earlier automation rules is available in the settings folder. Review it before restoring rules.
settings.automation_backup_error: Automation rules could not be backed up. Save a copy before installing an older version.
settings.title: Settings
settings.auto_start_hint: Open WireGuide automatically when you log in to your computer.
settings.compact_list_hint: Hide server addresses and reduce spacing to show more tunnels.
settings.kill_switch_hint: Block traffic outside the VPN. Protection pauses during connection setup and reconnect, and ends when you quit the app.
settings.dns_protection_hint: Block DNS requests to servers not specified by connected tunnels. Applied automatically for full-tunnel connections on Windows.
settings.health_check_hint: Reconnect if no new handshake occurs for 180 seconds. Recommended for tunnels with PersistentKeepalive enabled. Time asleep does not count: the check pauses for 90 seconds after waking, and on macOS while no network is available. A tunnel that has never completed a handshake is reconnected only if it has sent traffic, at growing intervals (up to 48 minutes).
settings.pin_interface_hint: Keep routes to the VPN server on the current network adapter.
settings.tunnel_backend_hint: Userspace uses the bundled Wintun driver. Kernel uses the official WireGuardNT driver and may improve throughput. Applies only to new connections; connected tunnels keep their current engine.
settings.tunnel_backend_confirm_message: Switch to {engine}? Tunnels connected now keep their current engine; the new engine applies the next time they connect.
settings.about_desc: WireGuide is an open-source client for managing VPN tunnels with WireGuard configuration files.
settings.notify_auto_changes_hint: Show a system notification when a tunnel connects or disconnects without you using this app, for example through automation.
settings.auto_update_check_hint: Check for a new version once a day.
settings.load_failed: Could not load settings. Try again.
settings.save_failed: Could not save or apply the change. Try again.
settings.export_diagnostics_hint: Saves a zip with logs, redacted tunnel configs, DNS, routes and firewall state for bug reports. Private and preshared keys are never included.
settings.dns_protection_blocking: Active: all DNS is blocked except local resolvers.
settings.dns_protection_inactive: Not applied — split DNS or no DNS
settings.dns_protection_idle: Turned on. Nothing to protect until a tunnel with DNS servers connects.
settings.helper_reason_legacy: launchd did not hand over a socket; the helper listens on its own
settings.helper_old: This helper predates detailed status. Use Repair helper to update it.
settings.helper_repair_hint: Reinstalls WireGuide’s background helper if it is missing or not responding. This is the only action here that asks for your administrator password.
settings.helper_repair_confirm: This reinstalls the helper and asks for your administrator password. WireGuide explains why before the prompt appears. Your tunnels and settings are kept.
settings.helper_repair_busy: Disconnect all tunnels and cancel pending reconnects first: repairing the helper would drop them.
settings.automation_v3_recoverable: Rules for {names} use Wi-Fi name lists or connection type and were removed by an older version of WireGuide. A backup is available.
settings.reset_dns_hint: If DNS or the internet stays broken after a crash or disconnect, this removes everything WireGuide changed. Your tunnels and settings are kept.
settings.reset_dns_item_firewall: Remove WireGuide’s firewall rules (kill switch and DNS protection)
settings.reset_dns_item_recovery: Retry restoring the pre-VPN DNS settings now, if a restore is pending
settings.reset_dns_force: Disconnect all tunnels first (including pending reconnects)
settings.reset_dns_ks_off: Turn off the kill switch (otherwise it blocks all traffic again within seconds)
settings.reset_dns_refused_tunnels: Tunnels are connected or waiting to reconnect: {tunnels}. Choose to disconnect them first.
settings.reset_dns_refused_ks: Turn off the kill switch first: it would block all traffic again right after the reset.

confirm.delete_message: Delete “{name}” and cancel its pending reconnects and recovery. This cannot be undone.

tools.dns_leak_desc: Send test queries to the system’s configured DNS servers and check whether any server not specified by the tunnel responds. Tunnels with split DNS receive a configuration check only.
tools.dns_leak_safe: No DNS leak detected in this test.
tools.dns_leak_leaked: A DNS server not specified by the tunnel responded.
tools.dns_leak_split_failed: Could not complete the DNS check.
tools.route_desc: System network routes. Routes marked VPN use a tunnel interface.
tools.dns_leak_dig_note: Terminal tip: dig and nslookup bypass split-DNS resolvers, so private names can fail there even when the tunnel works. Use dscacheutil -q host -a name <name> or ping instead.
tools.dns_leak_linux_note: Terminal tip: use resolvectl query <name> to see which resolver answers a name.

conflict.title: Overlapping network routes
conflict.message: The tunnel’s routes overlap existing network routes. Connecting may affect traffic on other networks or VPNs.
conflict.address_message: A connected tunnel already uses the same interface Address. Two tunnels claiming one address can make routing ambiguous. You can disconnect it first, or connect anyway.

update.vpn_warning: Updating will disconnect the VPN and restart WireGuide.
update.dev_build_hint: Development builds do not check for updates automatically.

wifi_permission.title: Location Services required
wifi_permission.desc: Wi-Fi rules need permission to read the network name. Allow WireGuide in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services.
wifi_permission.desc_denied: Location Services is denied for WireGuide, so Wi-Fi names can't be read and 'is not' SSID rules stay on hold. Allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services.
wifi_permission.desc_restricted: Location Services is restricted on this Mac (for example by a profile), so WireGuide can't read Wi-Fi names and 'is not' SSID rules stay on hold.
wifi_permission.desc_not_determined: Location Services has not been allowed for WireGuide yet, so Wi-Fi names can't be read. Allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services.

automation.title: Automation
automation.hint: The first matching rule is applied, from top to bottom. Connecting or disconnecting manually pauses automation until the network changes.
automation.empty: No rules added. Add a rule to connect or disconnect this tunnel based on your network.
automation.cond_none_desc: Apply when no other rule matches
automation.drag_hint: Drag or use the up and down arrow keys to reorder
automation.mac_invalid: Enter a valid MAC address, such as b0:38:6c:54:8b:ab.
automation.subnet_invalid: Enter an IP range in CIDR format, such as 192.168.0.0/24.
automation.negated_hint: Apply only when the condition is known and differs from this value. Rule evaluation pauses while the network is being identified.

why.title: Automation status
why.net_unknown: Wi-Fi name unknown — Location Services may be off; "is not" rules hold
why.net_type_unknown: Network type unknown; "is not" rules hold
why.settling: settling, {n} s ("is not" rules on hold)
why.v_held: on hold — waiting for the network to settle or the Wi-Fi name to be known
why.v_paused_connected: paused — you connected it by hand; resumes when the network changes
why.v_paused_disconnected: paused — you disconnected it by hand; resumes when the network changes
why.v_overlap: not connecting — {cidr} overlaps your current LAN
why.v_blocked: not reconnecting — the routing-loop watchdog stopped this tunnel; connect it by hand to clear
why.v_no_match: no rule matches the current network
why.net_unknown_denied: Location Services denied for WireGuide — Wi-Fi names unknown, 'is not' SSID rules on hold
why.net_unknown_not_allowed: Location Services not yet allowed for WireGuide — Wi-Fi names unknown, 'is not' SSID rules on hold
why.net_unknown_roaming: Wi-Fi name momentarily unavailable (reconnecting or roaming) — 'is not' rules hold

automation.rules_changed_outside: Rules for {name} changed outside the app.
automation.ssid_tags_hint: Wi-Fi names. Press Enter or type a comma to add another; the rule matches any of them.
automation.medium_windows_note: Windows can’t detect the connection type, so this rule never applies here.

ping_health.title: Reconnect when unresponsive
ping_health.description: Reconnect this tunnel when every target fails for the chosen number of consecutive checks. A reply from any target keeps the connection active.
ping_health.targets_hint: Enter up to 5 IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, one per line. Each must be within this tunnel’s AllowedIPs and respond to ping.
ping_health.cooldown: Wait up to 3 seconds for replies. Reconnect attempts are at least 60 seconds apart. This runs separately from the connection check in Settings.

verify.title: Verify
verify.note: Read-only checks that run only when you click. Nothing runs automatically.
verify.hint_handshake_none: The peer has not answered. Check the endpoint, keys and firewall.
verify.hint_handshake_old: Idle tunnels only re-handshake when traffic flows or PersistentKeepalive is set.
verify.hint_route_overlap: Hosts on your local network in this range are reached through the tunnel, not directly.
verify.hint_route_missing: The route was not installed. Try reconnecting the tunnel.
verify.hint_route_other: Another interface or VPN owns this prefix.
verify.hint_resolver_missing: The system did not register the resolver. Try reconnecting the tunnel.
verify.hint_resolver_outside: Add the resolver address to AllowedIPs so queries travel through the tunnel.
verify.hint_ping_failed: The host is down, filtered, or not routed through the tunnel.
verify.hint_resolve_nxdomain: The resolver answered but does not know this name. Check the ~domain and the resolver.
verify.hint_resolve_timeout: No answer in time. The resolver may be unreachable through the tunnel.
verify.hint_resolve_failed: The name did not resolve. Check the resolver and routes.
verify.detail_route_unmanaged: Routes are not managed by WireGuide (Table = {table})
verify.detail_route_overlap: {cidr} via {iface}: this range overlaps your LAN ({addr}) and is routed into the tunnel
verify.detail_resolver_unsupported: Split DNS is not checked on this platform
verify.detail_resolver_scutil_failed: Could not read the DNS configuration ({err})
verify.detail_resolver_outside: {domain} -> {resolver}: resolver reached over the local network, not the tunnel
verify.detail_resolve_outside: {name} -> {addrs} ({ms} ms) {via}: resolver reached over the local network, not the tunnel
verify.hint_route_unmanaged: Table = off, so WireGuide installs no routes. Add them yourself.
verify.hint_resolver_mismatch: Another resolver is registered for this domain. Disconnect the tunnel or app that owns it.
verify.detail_resolver_mismatch: {domain} -> {resolver}: not one of this tunnel's DNS servers
verify.detail_route_table: Routes are installed in table {table} (not checked)
verify.hint_route_table: WireGuide adds the ip rule that selects this table only for full-tunnel (0.0.0.0/0) configs. Otherwise add one yourself, e.g. ip rule add to <prefix> table <N>.

critical.dns_protection_failing: DNS protection is turned on but its firewall rules keep failing to apply, so DNS may not be locked to your tunnel.
critical.dns_protection_failing_hint: WireGuide keeps retrying. Settings > Advanced shows the current state and the last error.

preview.title: What will change when you connect
preview.dns_global_mac: Replaces DNS on all network services with {servers}.
preview.dns_split: Adds resolver {servers} for {domains} only; system DNS unchanged.
preview.dns_split_unsupported: Connecting will FAIL: split DNS ({domains}) is not supported here.
preview.routes_full: Routes all traffic through the tunnel.
preview.routes_none: Table=off: installs no routes. Add them yourself.
preview.routes_overlap: {range} overlaps your current network ({network}) and will be routed into the tunnel; automation will not auto-connect this tunnel.

url_action.connect_message: A link or shortcut asked WireGuide to connect "{name}".
url_action.disconnect_message: A link or shortcut asked WireGuide to disconnect "{name}".

detail.remaining_failed: Still connected, nothing else was changed: {tunnels}
detail.kill_switch_failed: Kill switch setting is off, but removing it failed: {error}
detail.firewall_failed: Could not remove the firewall rules: {error}
detail.split_dns_failed: Could not remove split DNS entries: {error}
detail.dns_recovery_pending: Still pending for {tunnels}; the saved settings are kept and will be retried
